title: Stopping and starting: waqf and ibtida': rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 25 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Stopping and starting rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 25. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

blocks.h: How to stop on a word

head: Not this
This
rows: Breathing and restarting from the very next word, cutting the phrase
Go back to the start of the phrase so the meaning is whole

keywords.def: the stopping signs in the mushaf
a short pause without a breath

questions.a: waahidah: tanween dropped, ة read as haa.

questions.q: Waqf map (pupil PDF): mark the ayah ends and any waqf signs in 79:17 to 24, and write how each last word is said at a stop. Today's rota group recites 79:9 to 16.
questions.a: Ayah ends: طَغَىٰ، تَزَكَّىٰ، فَتَخْشَىٰ، ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ، وَعَصَىٰ، يَسْعَىٰ، فَنَادَىٰ، ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ: all end on an alif, so at the stop each is a natural madd of 2 counts.

questions.q: Extend: why is it wrong to stop on «فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ» (79:18) and restart at «إِلَىٰٓ»?
questions.a: The question is incomplete; restarting mid-phrase breaks the meaning.

questions.q: Stretch: explain the difference between waqf and saktah.
questions.a: Waqf: stop with a breath; saktah: a short pause without a breath, only where the mushaf marks it.

questions.q: The sign «لا» in the mushaf means ...
questions.a: A) do not stop here. «لا»: do not stop at this point.

questions.q: Think again: If you run out of breath in the middle of a long ayah, what should you do so the meaning is not spoiled?
questions.a: Stop on a complete word, breathe, then go back a word or two and restart where the meaning is sound.
